# 2. Environments {#sec-environments}

*A generated chapter. Everything below the first paragraph is produced from
the JSON extracts in `data/environments/` when the site is rendered.*

The platform has one environment per stage of the release path. Each is its
own Azure subscription and network, and each contains three workspaces. The
tables and lists in this chapter are generated from the environment
descriptions exported by the infrastructure pipeline, so they describe the
environments as they are, not as they were when someone last edited this
file.

```{python}
#| output: asis
from scripts.platformdata import load_environments, md_table

envs = load_environments()

print("## 2.1 Environments at a glance {#sec-environments-glance}\n")
print(md_table(
    ["Environment", "Region", "Subscription", "Workspaces"],
    [[e.name, e.region, f"`{e.subscription}`", ", ".join(w.name for w in e.workspaces)]
     for e in envs],
    caption="Environments and their workspaces",
    label="tbl-environments",
))
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
for e in envs:
    print(f"\n## 2.{envs.index(e) + 2} The {e.name} environment {{#sec-environments-{e.name}}}\n")
    print(f"{e.description}\n")
    print(md_table(
        ["Workspace", "Catalog", "Compute", "Purpose"],
        [[w.name, f"`{w.catalog}`", w.compute, w.purpose] for w in e.workspaces],
    ))
    if e.storage:
        print("\nStorage accounts: " + ", ".join(f"`{s}`" for s in e.storage) + ".")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
# A diagram generated from the data: an SVG in the house style, written to
# assets/ (with PDF and PNG copies for the other formats) so it can also be
# reused elsewhere — a wiki page, a Miro board.
from scripts.platformdata import environments_svg, write_diagram
image = write_diagram("architecture/assets/environments", environments_svg(envs))
print(f"![Environments and workspaces, drawn from the same data]({image}){{#fig-environments}}")
```
